mainTopic: Does יאוש give a thief ownership? רבי אלעזר, then the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a thief who slaughters or sells after יאוש.
overview: This amud asks whether a theft is normally assumed to bring יאוש בעלים, the owner giving up hope. רבי אלעזר proves that it does from the תורה's rule that a thief who slaughters or sells pays ארבעה וחמשה. Selling is compared to slaughtering, so the sale must be a real sale that works, even one made right away. רבי יוחנן objects from kidnapping, where there is no יאוש and yet the seller is liable. So רבי יוחנן holds that a thief who sells before יאוש is liable. After יאוש, רבי יוחנן still says liable, while ריש לקיש says exempt, because יאוש makes the animal the thief's own. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא about a stolen animal that was made הקדש. ריש לקיש explains that the owner made it holy, following the צנועין, and that the thief was already judged, so he owes כפל. The גמרא then asks what kind of trial this was, using רבא's rule that a thief who slaughters or sells after the court's order to return the animal counts as a גזלן. This question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An ordinary theft is assumed to bring the owner's despair
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר states that in a normal theft, we assume the owner has given up hope of getting his item back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that an ordinary theft is assumed to involve the owner's despair.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר states a general rule: unless we know otherwise, a stolen item's owner is assumed to have given up hope (יאוש). The word תדע also tells us that a proof is about to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a default assumption about the owner's state of mind. Normally we cannot know whether a particular owner despaired. This rule means we do not need to know, because we assume he did.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (this). It introduces a proof for what was just said.
An ordinary theft, with no special information about it
The owner's despair, when he gives up hope of getting the item back

phrases.english: Know that an ordinary theft
phrases.notes: These are still the words of רבי אלעזר, continuing from before.

phrases.english: is the owner's despair

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע שֶׁסְּתָם גְּנֵיבָה יֵאוּשׁ בְּעָלִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's discussion from the earlier part of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary theft is presumed to involve יאוש בעלים.

steps.title: Proof from the fourfold and fivefold payment for selling
steps.stepSummary: The תורה makes a thief who sells a stolen animal pay four or five times its value. A sale only works after יאוש, so the תורה must be assuming that יאוש has happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the תורה said that if he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays four or five times. But maybe the owner had not yet despaired! It must be because we say that an ordinary theft is the owner's despair.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר proves his rule from the פסוק about a thief who slaughters or sells a stolen ox or sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief's sale only takes effect after the owner gives up hope. Yet the תורה requires the payment without first asking whether the owner despaired. That shows the תורה simply assumes despair in every ordinary theft.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered or sold (the stolen animal)
The fourfold payment (for a sheep) and fivefold payment (for an ox)
Rather, is it not that... It introduces the only explanation left.

steps.confusionAlert: The line 'ודלמא לא אייאש' is not a new challenge from the גמרא. It is רבי אלעזר asking himself a question to show that his explanation is the only one that works.

phrases.english: For the Torah said:
he slaughtered or sold
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
But perhaps the owner did not despair!
Rather, is it not because we say:
an ordinary theft is the owner's despair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof promised by תדע.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ordinary theft is presumed to involve יאוש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק requiring ארבעה וחמשה for a thief who slaughtered or sold, without any check for יאוש.

steps.title: Maybe the payment applies even without despair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. Maybe the thief pays four or five times even if the owner did not despair and the sale did not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he pays even though the owner did not despair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's proof. It suggests that the payment does not depend on the sale actually working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's proof assumes that the תורה only fines a sale that takes effect. If the fine applies to any attempted sale, even one that failed, the פסוק proves nothing about יאוש.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִיָּיאַשׁ!
phrases.english: But perhaps he pays even though the owner did not despair!
phrases.notes: The words 'he pays' aren't written here. The גמרא assumes them from the payment in step 2.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִיָּיאַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hidden assumption behind the proof in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the fourfold and fivefold payment only applies to a sale that takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the payment applies even to a sale that failed, the פסוק does not show that יאוש is assumed.

steps.title: Selling is like slaughtering: the act must actually work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that selling is compared to slaughtering. Slaughtering is an act that truly works, so the sale must also be one that works. A sale before יאוש does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Don't think that! Selling is like slaughtering. Just as slaughtering is an act that has an effect, so too selling must be an act that has an effect. And if it was before despair, what effect did it have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge and defends רבי אלעזר's proof by comparing selling to slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts טבח and מכר side by side, so they are treated alike. When a thief slaughters, the animal is really killed, so his act truly works. The sale must likewise be a real, working sale, which is only possible after יאוש. That means the payment does not apply to a failed sale, and רבי אלעזר's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; don't think that
Similar to; it compares one case to another
His actions were effective; his act really worked

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, a thief pays ארבעה וחמשה for selling only when the sale actually works, just like slaughtering. Since the תורה makes him pay without checking, ordinary theft is presumed to involve יאוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the thief's sale must be one that takes effect. It is the reason a sale before יאוש would not bring the fourfold and fivefold payment.

phrases.english: They say: This cannot enter your mind;
it is similar to slaughtering
phrases.notes: The selling in the פסוק is being compared to the slaughtering, since the פסוק mentions them together.

phrases.english: just as slaughtering is where his actions were effective,
so too selling is where his actions were effective.
And if it was before despair, what did his actions accomplish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 and restores the proof in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק by comparing selling to slaughtering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The payment for selling might apply even to a sale that did not take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like slaughtering, the sale must actually work. That requires יאוש, so the proof that ordinary theft is presumed to involve יאוש stands.

steps.title: Maybe the תורה means a case where we know the owner gave up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again: perhaps the four- or five-times payment for selling applies only when we actually heard the owner give up hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the תורה is talking about a case where we heard that the owner gave up hope!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's proof again. Maybe the תורה's case is only one where we actually know the owner gave up hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that the sale must be one that works, so it must happen after יאוש. But that does not prove every theft comes with יאוש. Maybe the תורה's law is limited to a case where we heard the owner say he gave up.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is where we heard him give up hope!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 showed the sale must work, this step suggests the תורה could be talking only about a special case of known יאוש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's proof that a normal theft comes with יאוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה's law might cover only a narrow case where we know the owner despaired. That would not show that יאוש is assumed in every theft.

steps.title: Selling is like slaughtering, which can happen right away
steps.stepSummary: The answer: selling is compared to slaughtering. Just as the thief can slaughter right away, the תורה also covers a sale made right away, before anyone could know about יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: You cannot think that. Selling is like slaughtering. Just as slaughtering can happen right away, selling also happens right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The sale in the תורה includes one done immediately after the theft, so the תורה is not limited to a case where we heard the owner give up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief is liable for slaughtering even if he does it right after stealing. Since selling is compared to slaughtering, a quick sale must also bring liability. A quick sale can only work if יאוש already happened, so the תורה assumes the owner gives up right away, and רבי אלעזר's proof stands.

phrases.english: They say: It cannot enter your mind;
it is similar to slaughtering –
phrases.notes: This is the same comparison of selling to slaughtering from step 4.

phrases.english: just as slaughtering is right away,
so too selling is right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5, using the same comparison as step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to slaughtering shows the תורה covers an immediate sale
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תורה's law might apply only when we know the owner gave up hope.
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling, like slaughtering, can happen right away. So the תורה assumes יאוש comes right after a normal theft.
steps.whatToRemember: Because selling is compared to slaughtering, the תורה includes a sale done right away. That supports רבי אלעזר: the owner gives up hope right away.

steps.title: Kidnapping shows a sale can bring liability without יאוש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי אלעזר: a kidnapper who sells a person is liable, even though no one gives up hope on his own freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Kidnapping proves the point. There is no owner's giving up, and yet he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks רבי אלעזר's whole proof with a counter-example from kidnapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's proof depended on the idea that a sale only brings liability if it works, so it must come after יאוש. With kidnapping, there is no יאוש, so the sale does not work, yet the תורה makes the kidnapper liable for selling. So a sale can bring liability even when it does not work, and the proof falls.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not arguing about kidnapping itself. He uses kidnapping only to show that selling can bring liability even when the sale does not work.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אלעזר, whose proof is being challenged.

phrases.english: stealing a person will prove it –
for there is no owner's despair, and yet he is liable!
phrases.notes: A person never gives up on his own freedom, so the kidnapper's sale never truly works.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גְּנֵיבָה בְּנֶפֶשׁ תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא defended the proof in step 6, רבי יוחנן attacks it with a case from a different area.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea in steps 2 and 4 that a sale brings liability only if it works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With kidnapping, the sale never works because there is no יאוש, yet the seller is liable. So liability for selling does not require a working sale.

steps.title: So רבי יוחנן holds a thief who sells before יאוש is liable
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's challenge, the גמרא learns his own view: a thief who sells a stolen animal before יאוש pays four or five times.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn from this that רבי יוחנן holds: before יאוש, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about רבי יוחנן's own opinion from the challenge he just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sale without יאוש brings liability for kidnapping, then רבי יוחנן must think the same about a stolen animal. A thief who sells it before the owner gives up hope still pays four or five times.

keyTerms.meaning: From this we can learn, by inference
Before the owner gives up hope

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Yoḥanan holds:
before despair, he is liable.
phrases.notes: This is about a thief who sells a stolen animal, not the kidnapper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out רבי יוחנן's own ruling from his challenge in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוחנן, a thief who sells a stolen animal before יאוש pays four or five times.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says a sale before יאוש still brings liability, so liability does not depend on the sale working.

steps.title: What about selling after the owner gave up hope?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the next question: if the thief sells after יאוש, is he liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: After the owner gives up hope, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question. Now that we know רבי יוחנן's view before יאוש, what happens after יאוש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the animal clearly still belongs to the owner. After יאוש, the thief may have gained some ownership, so maybe it no longer counts as selling something stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: After the owner gives up hope

phrases.english: After despair, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing liability before יאוש, the גמרא asks about after יאוש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a thief who sells or slaughters after יאוש pays four or five times.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says liable, ריש לקיש says exempt
steps.stepSummary: Two answers: רבי יוחנן says the thief is liable, and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: He is liable. ריש לקיש says: He is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a dispute between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן keeps the thief liable even after יאוש. ריש לקיש frees him. Their reasons come in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: He is liable,
and Reish Lakish says: He is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חַיָּיב, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: liable after יאוש. ריש לקיש: exempt after יאוש.

steps.title: The reasons behind each view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds the thief is liable both before and after יאוש. ריש לקיש holds that after יאוש the thief owns the animal, so he is slaughtering or selling his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says liable: his liability applies both before and after יאוש. ריש לקיש says exempt: his liability is only before יאוש. After יאוש he has acquired it, so he slaughters his own animal and sells his own animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each אמורא means, filling in the reasoning behind the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, יאוש makes no difference to the four or five times payment. For ריש לקיש, יאוש makes the animal belong to the thief, and nobody pays a penalty for selling or slaughtering his own animal. So the whole dispute is about whether יאוש turns the stolen animal into the thief's property.

keyTerms.meaning: He has acquired it, it is now his

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the thief pays four or five times whether he sells before or after יאוש. ריש לקיש: after יאוש the thief owns the animal, so he is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute shows the main question of the סוגיא: does יאוש alone give the thief ownership of the stolen item?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says liable –

phrases.aramaic: חִיּוּבֵיהּ בֵּין לִפְנֵי יֵאוּשׁ, בֵּין לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ.
phrases.english: his liability is both before despair and after despair.
Reish Lakish says exempt –
his liability is only before despair,
but after despair – he has acquired it,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלּוֹ הוּא טוֹבֵחַ וְשֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מוֹכֵר.
phrases.english: and it is his own that he slaughters, and his own that he sells.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר חַיָּיב – חִיּוּבֵיהּ בֵּין לִפְנֵי יֵאוּשׁ, בֵּין לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two rulings stated in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: liable before and after יאוש. ריש לקיש: after יאוש the thief owns the animal and is exempt.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא: a thief who stole, made the animal הקדש, and then slaughtered it pays double but not four or five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: If someone stole an animal, made it holy, and afterward slaughtered it, he pays double but does not pay four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש. Right now he is only quoting the source. The next steps explain why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the thief pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה once the animal became הקדש. רבי יוחנן will use this ruling to show that יאוש does not make the animal the thief's.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it holy, dedicating it to the בית המקדש
Double payment that a thief pays

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
If one stole and consecrated it,
and afterward slaughtered it —
he pays the double payment,
but he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's view from Step 11 that the thief is exempt after יאוש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that יאוש makes the stolen animal the thief's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up: the ברייתא's ruling will be shown to assume the thief is liable after יאוש.

steps.title: When did this happen? It cannot be before יאוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the ברייתא's case took place. It rules out 'before יאוש', because a thief cannot make an animal holy if it is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did this happen? If you say before the owner gave up hope, can it even become holy? The תורה says 'When a man makes his house holy.' Just as his house belongs to him, anything he makes holy must belong to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing down the case in the ברייתא. It throws out the 'before יאוש' option. This sets up the real challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the animal still fully belongs to the owner. The פסוק teaches that you can only make holy what is yours. So the thief's הקדש would not work at all, and the ברייתא must be talking about after יאוש.

keyTerms.term: מָה בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ אַף כֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Just as his house is his, so too anything he makes holy must be his

phrases.english: When did this happen?
If we say before the owner gave up hope,
is it holy at all?!
"When a man shall sanctify his house to be holy"
the Merciful One said —
just as his house belongs to him,
so too anything he consecrates must belong to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes when the ברייתא from Step 12 took place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא's case is before or after יאוש
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not before יאוש, since a thief cannot make holy what is not his

steps.title: After יאוש the thief still pays four or five, against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The case must be after יאוש. The ברייתא exempts him from four or five only because of the הקדש. So without it he would pay, which means יאוש does not give him ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it must be after יאוש. The only reason he does not pay four or five is that he made it holy, so he was slaughtering holy property. But if he had not made it holy and slaughtered it, he would pay four or five. If you think יאוש makes it his, why would he pay? He is slaughtering his own animal, selling his own animal!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main punch of רבי יוחנן's challenge. The ברייתא shows that after יאוש, a thief who slaughters pays four or five, which contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's exemption comes only from the הקדש. That means a plain thief who slaughters after יאוש would pay four or five. If ריש לקיש were right that יאוש makes the animal the thief's, there would be nothing to pay for.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy property belonging to the בית המקדש
The owner's giving up hope makes the thief the owner

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of the מחלוקת: does יאוש by itself make the stolen item the thief's?

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is after the owner gave up hope;
and the reason is only because he consecrated it
that he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי קָא טָבַח – דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ קָא טָבַח,
phrases.english: since when he slaughtered, he slaughtered consecrated property,
but if he did not consecrate it —
and he slaughtered, he would pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.
And if it enters your mind that the owner's despair acquires it for the thief,
why does he pay?
It is his own that he slaughters,
it is his own that he sells!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ יֵאוּשׁ קוֹנֶה, אַמַּאי מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'after יאוש' conclusion from Step 13 to finish רבי יוחנן's attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that after יאוש the thief owns the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies a thief slaughtering after יאוש without הקדש pays four or five. That is impossible if יאוש makes the animal his own.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the owner made it holy while it was with the thief
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא is before יאוש, and it was the owner, not the thief, who made the animal holy while it was in the thief's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? Where the owner made it holy while it was in the thief's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge by changing who made the animal holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner made it holy, it works even before יאוש, because it still belongs to him. So the ברייתא is a 'before יאוש' case and says nothing about after יאוש. ריש לקיש's view survives.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A way of narrowing a source to a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש reads the ברייתא as a case where the owner made the animal holy before יאוש. That way it does not prove the thief pays after יאוש.
steps.confusionAlert: The word הקדיש in the ברייתא sounded like the thief made it holy. ריש לקיש reads it as the owner doing so.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where the owner consecrated it
while it was in the thief's possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (אוקימתא): the owner made the animal holy, not the thief
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thief made the animal holy, so the case had to be after יאוש
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner made it holy before יאוש, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about after יאוש

steps.title: Can the owner even make a stolen animal holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's answer. It cites רבי יוחנן's ruling that before יאוש, neither the thief nor the owner can make a stolen item הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does it really become holy? But רבי יוחנן said: if someone stole, and the owners have not given up hope, neither of them can make it holy. The thief can't, because it is not his. The owner can't, because it is not in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's answer from Step 15. How could the owner make the animal holy while the thief had it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the owner made the animal הקדש before יאוש. רבי יוחנן rules that before יאוש the owner cannot do this, because the animal is not in his רשות. If that is true, the case ריש לקיש described could never happen.

keyTerms.meaning: To make something holy (הקדש), dedicating it to the בית המקדש
The owners gave up hope of getting the item back (יאוש)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different reasons here. The thief lacks ownership ("not his"). The owner lacks possession ("not in his רשות"). Each one is missing something different.

phrases.english: And does it become holy?!
phrases.notes: "It" is the animal the owner made holy while it was still with the thief, as ריש לקיש just said.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
If one stole and the owners have not given up hope,
neither of them is able to make it holy:
this one, because it is not his,
and that one, because it is not in his possession!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of ריש לקיש in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the owner made the animal הקדש before יאוש while it was in the thief's hands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules that before יאוש the owner cannot make a stolen item holy, because it is not in his possession. So the case ריש לקיש proposed is impossible.

steps.title: ריש לקיש follows the view of the צנועין
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that ריש לקיש's case follows the צנועין, who disagree with רבי יוחנן and hold that an owner can act on his item even when it is not in his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: he said it according to the view of the pious ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. It says his case is based on a different opinion, the view of the צנועין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not have to accept רבי יוחנן's rule. There is an earlier source, the צנועין, that holds an owner can still affect his item even when it is out of his possession. The next step brings that source.

keyTerms.meaning: The pious, careful people who were extra strict about הלכה

phrases.english: They say:
He said it according to the pious ones,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the position to a different תנאי opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agrees with רבי יוחנן that an owner cannot make a stolen item holy before יאוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש follows the צנועין, who hold that an owner can act on his item even when it is out of his possession.

steps.title: The source: the צנועין redeem fruit others might pick
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה showing that the צנועין redeemed fruit that passersby might take. So they held an owner can affect his property even after it leaves his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the pious ones would set aside coins and say: anything picked from this vine shall be redeemed onto these coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows what the צנועין held. This supports the answer in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit that passersby already picked is no longer in the owner's hands. Even so, the צנועין redeemed it, so they held the owner can still act on it. In the same way, an owner could make a stolen animal holy, which is what ריש לקיש needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeemed; the holiness is moved off the fruit onto the money

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
The pious ones would set aside coins,
and say: "Anything picked from this
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about a vine in its fourth year, whose grapes must be redeemed before they can be eaten outside ירושלים.

phrases.english: shall be redeemed onto these coins."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the answer in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion (the צנועין) allowing an owner to act on property no longer in his possession.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מעשר שני 5:1: the צנועין redeemed fruit that passersby would take.

steps.title: If the owner made it holy, hasn't the animal returned to him?
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge to ריש לקיש: by making the animal holy, the owner used his ownership, so the animal counts as returned to him. Then why should the thief pay כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the stolen item itself has returned to the owners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second problem with ריש לקיש's case. If the owner made the animal holy, it is as if he got it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the thief pays כפל. But once the owner acted on the animal as his own, the stolen item counts as returned. A thief whose stolen item has gone back to the owner should not pay כפל, so the ברייתא seems to contradict ריש לקיש's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal: the stolen item itself
The double payment a thief pays

phrases.english: But the principal has returned to the owners!
phrases.notes: By making the animal holy, the owner acted as its owner, so it counts as back with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending ריש לקיש on the question of making the animal holy, the גמרא raises a new difficulty with his case.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's case, where the owner made the animal holy, together with the ברייתא's ruling that the thief pays כפל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making the animal holy means the owner effectively got it back. Once the stolen item is returned, the thief should not owe כפל, yet the ברייתא says he pays it.

steps.title: The thief was already judged before the owner made it holy
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the thief had already stood trial and been found guilty before the owner made the animal holy, so the כפל was already owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he already stood in judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a timing detail. The court case happened first, and the owner made the animal holy afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thief's duty to pay כפל was fixed when בית דין judged him. The owner made the animal holy only later, so the return of the item cannot cancel a debt that was already set. This keeps ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood in judgment; was tried and found guilty in בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: So far, ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא is this: before יאוש, the owner made the animal holy (following the צנועין), and the thief pays כפל because he was judged first. The next step challenges this answer by asking what kind of trial it was.

phrases.english: Where he stood in judgment.
phrases.notes: The thief had already been tried and found guilty before the owner made the animal holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the owner made the animal holy before the trial, which would cancel the כפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The trial came first, so the כפל was already owed before the animal returned to the owner.

steps.title: What kind of trial was it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the trial looked like. If the court had already said "צא תן לו", why does the case need הקדש? Even without הקדש the thief should be exempt from ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly was the case? If the court told the thief "Go, give it back to him," why mention that the owner made it holy? Even if he did not make it holy, the thief should still not have to pay ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 20, that the thief had already stood trial. It asks what kind of trial that was, and shows that one possible answer makes the הקדש detail pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case being discussed says the thief is exempt from ארבעה וחמשה because the owner made the animal הקדש. But if the court had already ordered "צא תן לו", the thief would be exempt anyway, as the next step will show. So the הקדש would not be the reason for the exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: "Go, give it to him": the court's final order to return the item
He made it holy (dedicated it to the בית המקדש)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the כפל here. It is asking why the הקדש is needed to explain the exemption from ארבעה וחמשה.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If it is where they said: "Go, give it to him"
Why specifically where he consecrated it?
Even if he did not consecrate it
the thief should also not be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּאָמְרִי צֵא תֵּן לוֹ מַאי אִירְיָא הִקְדִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20 by asking what kind of trial it was.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 20 that the thief had already stood trial before the הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the trial ended with the court ordering "צא תן לו", the thief is exempt from ארבעה וחמשה without any הקדש. That makes the הקדש detail unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא's ruling after the court orders return
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבא's rule as the source for the challenge. If the court said "צא תן לו" and the thief then slaughtered or sold the animal, he is exempt. Then it asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: if the court told the thief "Go, give it back," and he then slaughtered or sold it, he is exempt. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ruling of רבא. It ends by asking for the reason, which sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling shows that a thief who slaughters or sells after the court's "צא תן לו" is exempt from ארבעה וחמשה. This is exactly what makes the הקדש detail unnecessary in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered or sold (the acts that make a thief owe ארבעה וחמשה)

phrases.english: As Rava said:
If the court said "Go, give it to him," and he slaughtered or sold it, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Exempt from the four- or five-times payment.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the assumption behind the challenge in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that after "צא תן לו" the thief is exempt from ארבעה וחמשה even without הקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling: if the court said "צא תן לו" and the thief then slaughtered or sold the animal, he is פטור.

steps.title: After the ruling the thief becomes a robber
steps.stepSummary: The reason: once the court has decided his case, slaughtering or selling turns him into a גזלן, and a גזלן does not pay ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the court already decided his case, and then he slaughtered or sold the animal, he counts as a robber. A robber does not pay ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבא's ruling. It finishes the support for the challenge of step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra payments of ארבעה וחמשה apply only to a גנב, someone who steals in secret. After the court has ruled and he still holds on to the animal and slaughters or sells it, the law treats him as a גזלן. A גזלן never pays ארבעה וחמשה, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: They decided his matter (the court gave a final ruling)
A robber, who takes openly and by force
The four- or five-times payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox

steps.whatToRemember: After the court says "צא תן לו", a thief who slaughters or sells the animal counts as a גזלן and pays no ארבעה וחמשה. So if step 20's trial reached that point, the הקדש would add nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: A גנב steals in secret and a גזלן takes openly. Only a גנב pays כפל and ארבעה וחמשה, which is why becoming a גזלן here leads to an exemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule puts pressure on the answer from step 20. It forces the סוגיא to define the trial differently.

phrases.english: Since the court decided his matter
and he then slaughtered or sold it
he is considered a robber
and a robber does not pay
the four- or five-times payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the "מאי טעמא" question at the end of step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a thief who slaughters or sells after "צא תן לו" is exempt.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Once the court has ruled, slaughtering or selling makes him a גזלן, and a גזלן does not pay ארבעה וחמשה.
